name: Pimenteira
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Cariban of Piaui; Glottolog cites only Martius 1867 wordlist material and subclassification notes; no phonology exists.

sources.note: Nothing; stub stating the language is known only from the Martius wordlist (published 1863), extinct c. 1827, name is Portuguese, original name unknown; cites Loukotka 1955/1968, Rodrigues 1985, Steward 1946, Martius 1867.

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain. 2005-. Diccionario etnolingüístico y guía bibliográfica de los pueblos indígenas sudamericanos: Caribe (online PDF).
sources.note: Nothing; Pimenteira appears only as an extinct member in the reproduced classifications (Kaufman, Durbin, Loukotka); no bibliography entry of its own.

sources.citation: Rodrigues, Aryon D. 1985. Evidence for Tupi-Carib relationships. In Harriet E. Manelis Klein & Louisa R. Stark (eds.), South American Indian Languages: Retrospect and Prospect, 371-404. Austin: University of Texas Press.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.locator: printed p. 373 and note 3, printed p. 398
sources.note: This work describes Comparative Tupi vs Carib (Tupinamba, Tupari, Munduruku vs Waiwai, Hixkaryana, Taulipang, Galibi, Wayana, Makushi, Bakairi, Nahukwa, Island Carib); Pimenteira is mentioned only as a Carib isolate in the classification survey. The work says nothing about word stress, accent or tone in Pimenteira or in any other language. It is a comparative Tupi-Carib paper: classification survey (pp. 371-373), Table I consonant correspondences (p. 377ff.), List A cognate sets with grammatical morphemes and lexicon, Lists B-C loanwords, discussion of Macro-Je and Greenberg's grouping (pp. 3…

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1955. Les langues non-Tupí du Brésil du Nord-Est. In Herbert Baldus (ed.), Anais do XXXI Congresso Internacional de Americanistas (São Paulo, 1954), vol. II, pp. 1029-1054. São Paulo: Anhembi. Pimenteira paragraph pp. 1044-1045.
sources.note: Nothing; states that Martius (t. II, pp. 219-220) left the only specimen of the language, that the tribe died out c. 1827, and that Adam established its Cariban affiliation.

sources.citation: Adam, Lucien. 1893. Matériaux pour servir à l'établissement d'une grammaire comparée des dialectes de la famille caribe. Paris: Maisonneuve (Bibliothèque linguistique américaine 17).
sources.note: Nothing on Pimenteira stress; lists 'Pimenteiras. Rio Piauhy. Martius. Vocab. inséré dans son ouvrage' as a source and cites a few Pimenteira forms (sôba-rôh 'bras', angutu, incau) in comparative morphology; no accent statement found by a full-text search for stress/accent.

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, Bd. I: Zur Ethnographie. Leipzig: Fleischer. Pimenteiras pp. 348-350.
sources.note: Nothing; ethnographic/historical note on the Pimenteiras (location at Lagoa das Pimenteiras, raids from 1775), no language data.

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1863. Glossaria linguarum Brasiliensium. Glossarios de diversas lingoas e dialectos, que fallao os Indios no imperio do Brazil. Wörtersammlung brasilianischer Sprachen. Erlangen: Junge (re-issued 1867 as Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, Bd. II). Pimenteira wordlist pp. 219-220.
sources.note: Nothing. A c. 120-item Latin-Pimenteira wordlist 'von uns in Piauhy aufgenommen' with a footnote noting resemblance to Cayriri and Tamanaco; some forms carry acute/circumflex diacritics (cojabó, kuckú, oráh, jéjé, marabú, tschiaungâh) but no statement about Pimenteira stress; the introduction's orthographic note (about Tupi spelling) says the acute 'dient, den Vocal zu schärfen oder die Sylbe zu betonen'.
sources.venue: Glossarios de diversas lingoas e dialectos, que fallao os Indios no imperio do Brazil
